title: Compatibility of Picard restriction with H^1 of units
statement: For a closed immersion i:Z\to X of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], the square formed by the pullback map on isomorphism classes of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], L \mapsto i^*L [def-pc-module-pullback], and the map H^1(X_{\rm Zar},O_X^*) \to H^1(X_{\rm Zar},i_*O_Z^*) = H^1(Z_{\rm Zar},O_Z^*) induced by O_X^* \to i_*O_Z^* and the closed-immersion cohomology identification [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] commutes with the isomorphisms of [thm-sc-hilbert-90] (equivalently, the class of L maps to the class of i^*L). Here H^1 is the cohomology of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] on the small Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site], and O_X^* is viewed as the units torsor sheaf [def-sc-gm-torsor]; Picard groups use [def-sc-picard-group].

source.place: Lemma 09NY proof, final sentence, together with Cohomology Lemma 02UV and Lemma 09NU

proof.text: Obtain the canonical isomorphism from abstract module pullback to tensorPullback from uniqueness of left adjoints of pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback]. Abstract pullback preserves invertibility; transport along this isomorphism to supply the invertibility witness for tensorPullback. The Hilbert-90 formula [thm-sc-hilbert-90], Pic.toH1Units_mk, identifies both classes with generator-torsor classes.

Construct the equivariant map from the generator torsor of L to the explicit direct-image generator torsor of tensorPullback(i,L). On U it sends s to e.hom.app(i^{-1}U)(pullbackSection i s). The proved IsFreeGenerator.pullback_unit_app and IsFreeGenerator.app_hom show it is a generator; Hom.app_presheaf_map with pullbackSection_map prove naturality; pullbackSection_smul with Hom.app_smul prove equivariance along unitsSheafToPushforward. Apply the proved Sheaf.Torsor.classH1_eq_map_of_equivariant to identify the H^1 image class.

Apply [lem-sc-units-torsor-closed-restriction-class] to the generator torsor on Z. Rewrite its equality and use the equivariant-map equality from step 2. This proves the requested square with unchanged hypotheses and conclusion.
